title: Consolidated routing & client compatibility spec for batch embeddings migration
creator: Aisha Khan
description: This ticket defines the product requirements and migration plan to consolidate legacy batch embeddings endpoints into the new unified embeddings API. It covers routing policies, compatibility shims for SDKs, client guidance, acceptance criteria, and a phased timeline to minimize customer disruption. The goal is to remove duplicate endpoints that increase maintenance cost and inconsistent request semantics while preserving per-customer throughput and latency characteristics.
background: Historically we offered two batch embeddings interfaces: /v0/embeddings/batch (legacy) and /v1/embeddings (new unified). Clients have differing integration patterns: some send very large batches (>=1024 vectors), others stream smaller batches. The runtime now supports a single endpoint with per-call 'batch_mode' hints, and improved routing kernels. Consolidation reduces surface area and enables smarter routing and batching optimizations, but requires a careful client migration path to avoid regressions.
goals: Provide a clear, minimum-disruption migration path for customers using legacy batch endpoints
Enable routing by profile (low-latency vs high-throughput) using a single endpoint
Ship SDK compatibility shims and server-side fallback for at least one release cycle
Define acceptance criteria and monitoring to detect quality, latency, and cost regressions
Complete the first production deprecation window and migrate >90% of active keys within 8 weeks of announcement
scope_in_scope: Deprecation plan for /v0/embeddings/batch and associated model aliases
Server-side routing policy: route requests with 'batch_hint' to dedicated high-throughput pools
SDK changes: compatibility shims that translate legacy request shape to new API
Client guidance: migration guide, code examples, and recommended parameter mappings
Instrumentation and dashboards to measure latency P50/P95/P99, tokens-per-second, and cost-per-vector
scope_out_of_scope: Changes to embedding model architectures or training data
On-prem packaging for customers requiring offline upgrades (will be tracked in Private roadmap)
Major runtime kernel rewrites — performance tweaks only as part of routing configuration
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility shim in SDKs (Python/Node/Go) translates legacy batch payloads to /v1/embeddings without changing vector outputs
Server accepts legacy header X-Embeddings-Batch-Version=0 and returns a 200 with a migration-warning header for 60 days
Dashboard shows stable P95 latency for migrated customers within +/-10% of baseline
Automated canary tests covering small-batch, large-batch (>1024), and mixed-concurrency workloads pass in staging
Migration documentation published and linked from Console; support playbook created
>90% of active API keys that used /v0/batch have been observed calling /v1/embeddings or using the SDK shim before the hard cutoff
migration_steps: Week 0 — Announcement: publish migration blog + console banner indicating deprecation window and resources
Week 1 — SDK shims release (Python v2.7.1, Node v1.9.4, Go v0.5.2) that log a single migration-warning per session and translate payloads
Week 2 — Server routing update: accept legacy path and route requests to correct pools; start emitting metric 'legacy_batch_migrated'
Week 2–4 — Invite top-50 customers to join migration pilot; provide dedicated support and run performance baselines
Week 5 — Start progressive rate-limited 400 responses for unknown legacy clients that still hit /v0/batch (soft enforcement), continue SDK shim support
Week 8 — Hard cutoff: reject /v0/embeddings/batch with 410 Gone; offer a migration endpoint that returns mapping instructions
Post-cutoff — 4-week remediation window with support-assisted migrations and SLA credits for verified regressions
client_guidance_summary: Map POST /v0/embeddings/batch body -> POST /v1/embeddings with 'inputs' array; set 'batch_hint' to 'large' if >256 vectors
If clients rely on streaming for partial results, recommend 'stream_chunks=true' and 'prefetch=1' to preserve latency characteristics
For clients that expect identical vector outputs, ensure model alias is pinned (e.g., 'embed-1.0' in model field) during migration

def migrate_payload(legacy_payload):
    return {'model': legacy_payload.get('model_alias', 'embed-1.0'), 'inputs': legacy_payload['vectors'], 'batch_hint': 'large' if len(legacy_payload['vectors'])>256 else 'small'}
Advise SDK users to upgrade to the shimed SDK before server-side cutoff to avoid failed requests
rollout_timeline: 2026-03-15 — Public deprecation announcement and docs published
2026-03-22 — Server accepts legacy requests with warning header
2026-04-05 — Begin soft enforcement (400 responses for non-upgraded clients after rate limit threshold)
rollback_plan: If we observe a significant spike in errors (>5% of total embedding requests) or P95 latency regression >20% for migrated traffic, we will: 1) revert server-side hard enforcement immediately (restore /v0/embeddings/batch acceptance), 2) roll back routing policy changes that moved traffic to high-throughput pools, and 3) open a hotfix release to update the SDK shim. Decision window: 30 minutes of elevated error/latency after alerting. Communication: Postmortem and status updates to affected customers within 4 hours.
monitoring_and_metrics: alert: legacy_batch_requests > 5% of baseline after cutoff -> high-priority pager
dashboard: migration progress % of active keys migrated; top 20 keys still calling legacy endpoint
